It returns through the journey's own /address-return on the animals frontend, carrying the fulfilment id, the token, the new address id and a landing, to the page each button names: 'Save and select' commits the copy and lands on the Consignment addresses page, 'Save and return to address page' lands on the picker unselected, and 'Cancel and return to hub' is a link that saves nothing. conflicts.outcome: The prototype's edit form cannot express either case: its country list is fixed, so no stored code is ever missing from it, and it never refuses a save. The 7 October ruling's validation and persistence clause settles both. The select offers no blank option while the stored country is one the list offers, which is Design Release 2.1's look; where the stored code is not offered the select opens blank rather than silently showing another country, and that blank state is what 'Select a country' refuses on save (req-1234). Nothing is overruled: the prototype still decides the select's look for every address whose country MDM still serves.

conflicts.about: Whether the address book's add-details step asks for a county.

positions.says: The address book's add-details step keeps its County field; it is not removed.
This decision replaces inc-062's criterion that the add-details step has no County field.
County is a field of the Standard Address Block, marked Optional.
The Design Release 2.1 add-details step has no County field, unlike the root address book manual fields.
The add-details form carries a County field, marked optional, between Town or city and Postcode or Zip code.

conflicts.outcome: Paul's ruling of 14 October ranks above the prototype and keeps County on the add-details step, labelled 'County (optional)' between 'Town or city' and 'Postcode or Zip code' (req-address-book-add-and-edit-009). Its grounds are the V4 Address Block, which gives every address block the same fields with County among them and outranks the prototype, and the round trip: an add form that cannot set a field the record, the view page and the edit form all carry would lose it. Design Release 2.1 leaving the field out is therefore a prototype mistake, and prototype-dr2-1-source-p16-045 is set aside; req-1225, which asked for the field to go, is out of scope and keeps the claim as the record of what was set aside. The ruling is marked to confirm with Sam and gives no format or limit, so the field keeps the 100-character cap the record and the edit form already enforce.

conflicts.about: Which environments' saved addresses are deleted when the address book starts storing roles, beyond dev, test and a local stack.

positions.says: The entire addresses collection is deleted on the two shared environments, dev and test, using CDP tooling, because none of the addresses already saved has any value.
Locally the stack is restarted instead of dropping a collection with CDP tooling.
The ruling says nothing about what happens to addresses saved before the change in any environment beyond dev, test and a local stack.
Roles are optional on the stored document, so a record can be held with none.

conflicts.outcome: Nothing ranks the readings: the ruling names dev, test and a local stack and is silent on every other environment, and a record saved before the change can still be held with no role at all, so an address without a role would reach a picker that filters by role. Each part of the target therefore gets what the default below says until the owner answers, and req-address-book-add-and-edit-005 waits on it.
conflicts.question: Besides dev, test and a local stack, which environments have their addresses collection dropped when the address book starts storing roles, and what happens to an address already saved there?
conflicts.default: After the change is released, dev and test have the whole addresses collection dropped with CDP tooling and the address book restarted, and a local stack is restarted. perf-test and ext-test are dropped the same way when the change reaches them, because their addresses are test data too. Pre-production and production are not touched and no address is deleted there, the service not being live for traders yet; if an address without a role is ever found in either, it is left in place and no picker offers it, rather than being deleted or given a role.

conflicts.about: Whether an add reached from a notification journey shows the roles question with the hand-off's role ticked, or hides it and applies that role on its own.

positions.says: Save and select on a journey hand-off stores the address and gives it the party's role without the user ticking any role, so a journey-reached add form does not ask the roles question the address-book-reached one does.
No spec proves whether an add form reached from a journey hand-off shows or hides the roles question, so the suite holds the service to nothing about it.
A journey section starting an address book add records where to return and suggests that section's address type.

conflicts.outcome: The tests repo says both things and proves neither: one claim reads the code as not asking the question, the other finds nothing that holds the service either way, and the prototype's journey add suggests a type without reaching the roles question at all. Nothing ranks the two readings and they build different pages, so it goes to the owner with the default below, and req-address-book-add-and-edit-006 waits on it.
conflicts.question: On an add reached from a notification journey, is the roles question shown with the hand-off's party role already ticked, or hidden with that role applied on save?
conflicts.default: The question is shown with the hand-off's party role ticked, so the page reads the same as the add reached from the address book and a trader adding, say, a consignor address that is also the place of origin can tick both before saving. The ticked role is kept whatever else the trader ticks, so the journey always gets an address it can select.
